transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... well, it feels a little silly even taking up your time with this, to be honest. I hope it's okay that I'm here. 

I'm just... I'm here because I have this thing about wasps, and I guess it's gotten to the point where I sort of plan my whole summer around avoiding them. It's not a huge deal, really, but I did end up giving up my volunteer garden jobs at the church because of it. And, oh gosh, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but if I hear even a little buzzing by the back porch, I'll actually make my husband unload the car and bring everything in. 

I know it sounds foolish for a grown woman to act like that, but I just can't seem to help it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm in the right place for this sort of thing.
Is your fear limited to wasps, or do you feel similarly anxious around other animals or insects as well?

Oh, um, no... it's really just the wasps. I mean, I don't exactly love spiders or anything, but they don't make me act all... unreasonable like that. Dogs, cats, even regular bumblebees, I'm perfectly fine with them. 

It's just those awful wasps. I hope that's okay? I know sometimes people are scared of a whole list of things, so I'm sorry if I'm not giving you very much to go on. But yes, just the wasps. Is that... is that normal for this kind of thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

latest_inference.note: The patient confirmed that the fear is specifically limited to wasps, ruling out other phobias and confirming the specific phobia, animal type.
